title: Recover Without Repairing or Replaying
learningGoals: Distinguish meaning repair from image repair

deeperExplanation.question: How is reflection different from replaying?
deeperExplanation.answer: Reflection has a question and an ending. You might ask what helped me return after a difficult word, write one observation and choose a small experiment. Replaying often seeks a past version you can no longer create or certainty about what everyone thought. When you notice the review has stopped producing useful information, close it. You can return later with a specific question if there is a reason.

sections.narration:
Welcome. Today we are exploring Recover Without Repairing or Replaying. A word is difficult, then the rest of the answer goes by while you are still mentally correcting it. Later you replay the whole conversation, hoping to find the version that should have happened.

In this session, we will distinguish meaning repair from image repair, return to the current exchange, and end a brief review. I will explain the idea, show a visual example, and invite you to try it in a small experience of your own. You can ask me a question or switch to reading at any point. We will finish by choosing what, if anything, you want to take into a real conversation.

sections.narration: Recovery means returning to what is happening now. You may need to repair meaning if the listener misunderstood. You do not have to repair every uneven sound or repeat a whole answer to prove you can say it smoothly. We will distinguish communication repair from image repair.

sections.narration:
A word is difficult, then the rest of the answer goes by while you are still mentally correcting it. Later you replay the whole conversation, hoping to find the version that should have happened.

After a difficult moment, ask a practical question: is something important unclear? If yes, clarify that part. If the message was understood, consider continuing. Later reflection can be useful when it is brief and leads to one experiment. Replaying for a different past outcome often has no natural stopping point.

sections.narration: Choosing not to repeat is not another strict rule. Sometimes repetition helps a listener or is simply natural. The point is to recognise when repair has become a test of your worth. A changed, unchanged or uncertain experience is information, not a grade. You do not have to report relief for this attempt to count as exploration.

sections.narration: After one difficult moment, check meaning once and return to the exchange. Save at most one observation for later practice. During focused practice, you can deliberately explore this one tool. In an everyday conversation, give most of your attention to the message and the other person. A familiar support can be available if it helps; you do not have to monitor the tool throughout the exchange.
